Flat Earth belief is less about geography and more about epistemology—how people believe they know what’s true. It’s driven by:

  • Misinterpretation of evidence through lay intuition

In that sense, Flat Earth is not an alternative model of the world—it’s a worldview that reorients the believer’s relationship with knowledge, authority, and identity.

  5. Religious or Philosophical Motivations — Some flat Earth beliefs intersect with literalist religious readings (e.g., interpretations of certain biblical passages describing a "firmament" or "ends of the earth").

Why These Arguments Persist Despite Evidence

Researchers in sociology and psychology identify several mechanisms:

  • Confirmation bias — Information supporting the model is embraced; contradictory evidence is reinterpreted as part of the conspiracy.
